label: r4c1
name: r3c2 + 32 minibatches
hypothesis: Same network and recipe as r3c2, but n_minibatches goes from 16 to 32. This doubles the gradient steps per update (128 samples per minibatch) at no counted compute cost, so the number of training samples is unchanged. Learning was still rising at the end, so faster learning from the same data should raise dev success and help the slow seed. Refuted if 2-seed dev success falls below about 0.55.
last_analysis: Lining the shifted target up with the build was the key fix: the X/2 shift-back took dev success from 0 to about 0.6. Passing the per-cell stem features into the footprint head (r3c2) gave the best result, 0.70 (seeds 0.50 and 0.90), but that gain is within seed noise. Seed spread is very large. Moving the recipe away from ppo_epochs 2 with the default gamma did worse: 1 epoch, gamma 0.99 and 2x more updates all scored lower, and a deeper trunk collapsed to instant DONE. Training success was still rising at the end of every good run. In r3c2's trace the agent stops before placing one 1x2 overhang brick that needs exact per-cell landing reasoning, which pooled max/min/mean features lose. Two cheap levers remain: more gradient steps on the same samples (smaller minibatches add no counted compute), and a head that sees each footprint cell's features separately.
